packages.label: מַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן וְהַנִּיצוֹצוֹת
packages.reason: The dominant concept is מַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן (commercial trade), which the Torah defines as בְּחִינוֹת שֶׁמְּנַשְּׂאִין וּמְרִימִין הַדָּבָר — literally the act of lifting and restoring things to their place. This is identified as the cosmic function of raising fallen holy sparks (ניצוצות). Commerce = עֲשִׂיָּה (the World of Action), which is the lowest spiritual level and the realm from which sparks must be lifted. The biblical phrase כִּי תֵצֵא (when you go out) maps onto commerce as the mode of 'going out' into the world — צֵאתְךָ — and Zevulun's verse שְׂמַח זְבוּלוּן בְּצֵאתֶךָ encapsulates the spirit of this domain. All nodes in this package share the essential nature of engaged outward activity in the material world whose inner purpose is the elevation of trapped holiness.
nodes: שמנשאין ומרימין הדבר, ונותנין ומשיבין אותו למקומו

merge_notes.reason: These two nodes are definitional synonyms of each other (the edge connecting them is a pure equivalence: 'fallen holiness, namely the fallen sparks'). Their thematic home is the commerce package because commerce is not merely the cause of their elevation — commerce IS defined as the bechina of lifting/raising (שֶׁמְּנַשְּׂאִין וּמְרִימִין), which means the sparks and the lifting activity share the same essential nature. The fallen sparks are the very substance of what commerce operates on; they belong inside the commerce package as the implicit object of its cosmic definition. Contrast with faith (Package 3), which PRODUCES the elevation (eitza) but does not share the same nature as the sparks themselves.

packages.label: תּוֹרָה וִיצִירָה
packages.label_en: Torah and the World of Formation
packages.reason: This package clusters around תּוֹרָה as the inner, higher dimension of spiritual life — the counterpart to the outer activity of commerce. The Torah is identified with the letter וָא

merge_notes.reason: The proof text reads 'עֲבוֹדַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת יִשָֹּשׂכָר בְּאֹהֳלֶיךָ' — Torah study IS the bechina of Issachar in the tents. This pair (Component D) belongs in the Torah package because its essential nature is identical: both nodes are expressions of deep Torah engagement as an inward spiritual mode. The Torah explicitly contrasts this with commerce (Zevulun = going out), placing Torah study in direct opposition as the 'higher' inward domain — the same domain as יצירה and וא

packages.label: אֱמוּנָה וִירוּשָׁלַיִם
packages.reason: This package clusters around אֱמוּנָה (faith/faithfulness) as the spiritual quality that dwells among the klipot and keeps the fallen sparks from being entirely lost. The key equation is: יְרוּשָׁלַיִם = קִרְיָה נֶאֱמָנָה = בְּחִינוֹת אֱמוּנָה. Jerusalem the 'faithful city' is a bechina of faith — they share the same essential quality of steadfast presence amid hostile surroundings. The Torah draws on the verse from Yechezkel (5:5): 'This is Jerusalem I have placed in the midst of the nations,' equating Jerusalem's location among the nations with faith's dwelling among the klipot. All three nodes (Jerusalem, faithful city, faith) are expressions of the same essential quality: unshakeable divine presence in an unredeemed world. Note: מַלְכוּת דַּעֲשִׂיָּה is explicitly identified in the source as 'the bechina of faith in commerce' (line 11 of the text) but this node is not in the dataset — see additions file.
